Helper Functions
```{r}
# ArcGIS includes Null for fields that don't exist, coerce those to NA to work in a tibble
nullToNA <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return(NA)
  x
}

# The JSON that is returned from the website is super messy and kept giving errors, this is to convert it all to the same format to reduce errors. Not all of this is strictly necessary as I kept adding things until it worked but it works now so I am not going to change it. 
normalizeAttributes <- function(items) {
  # Return NULL if the JSON object doesn't exist or is NULL in any way
  if (is.null(items) || length(items) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Converts messy JSON to a cleaner format: removing names, converting NULL values to NAs, flattening, and cooercing to characters anything that isn't NA
  scalarize <- function(x) {
    if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) {
      return(NA_character_)
    }

    if (is.atomic(x) && length(x) == 1) {
      return(as.character(x))
    }

    if (is.atomic(x) && length(x) > 1) {
      return(toJSON(unname(x), auto_unbox = TRUE))
    }

    return(toJSON(x, auto_unbox = TRUE, null = "null"))
  }

  # Apply the scalarize function to each of the nested JSON items in the items array
  out <- lapply(items, scalarize)

  # Convert the flattened and cleaned JSON to a tibble  
  as.data.frame(out, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}
```

Scraping Functions
```{r}
# Checks whether the requested URL is a dynamic layer query or a direct layer query
isDynamicQuery <- function(url) {
  str_detect(url, "dynamicLayer/query")
}

# Constructs a JSON object with the layer of interest on the arcgis map
makeLayerJson <- function(layer_id) {
  toJSON(
    list(source = list(type = "mapLayer", mapLayerId = layer_id)),
    auto_unbox = TRUE
  )
}

# Gets all of the IDS in the requested layer (all of the different properties)
getObjectIDs <- function(url, layerJson = NULL) {
  # Build the request body. Direct layer queries do not use the layer JSON object
  body <- list(
    where = "1=1",
    returnIdsOnly = "true",
    f = "json"
  )

  # Dynamic layer queries require the layer JSON object
  if (isDynamicQuery(url)) {
    body$layer <- layerJson
  }

  # Sends a request to the arcgis API for every ID and returns as a JSON object
  response <- POST(
    url,
    body = body,
    encode = "form",
    timeout(120),
    user_agent("Mozilla/5.0")
  )

  # Wait until the server gets a response and continues if it is a success or returns an R error if there is some error in the request
  stop_for_status(response)

  # Convert from JSON to an R object
  idsList <- fromJSON(content(response, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"), simplifyVector = FALSE)

  # If ArcGIS returns an error, stop and print that message
  if (!is.null(idsList$error)) {
    stop(idsList$error$message)
  }

  # Return a sorted array of the object IDs
  sort(as.integer(unlist(idsList$objectIds)))
}

# Fetch a chunk of object IDs, including geometry, and convert it to a flat data frame
fetchChunk <- function(url, chunk_id, out_fields = "*", layerJson = NULL) {
  # Build the request body. Direct layer queries do not use the layer JSON object
  body <- list(
    objectIds = paste(chunk_id, collapse = ","),
    outFields = out_fields,
    returnGeometry = "true",
    outSR = "4326",
    f = "json"
  )

  # Dynamic layer queries require the layer JSON object
  if (isDynamicQuery(url)) {
    body$layer <- layerJson
  }

  # Sends a single request to the arcgis API to return both attribute JSON and geometry JSON
  response <- POST(
    url,
    body = body,
    encode = "form",
    timeout(120),
    user_agent("Mozilla/5.0")
  )

  # Wait until the server gets a response and continues if it is a success or returns an R error if there is some error in the request
  stop_for_status(response)

  # Convert from JSON to an R object
  data <- fromJSON(content(response, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"), simplifyVector = FALSE)

  # If ArcGIS returns an error, stop and print that message
  if (!is.null(data$error)) {
    stop(data$error$message)
  }

  # Sometimes the server returns empty objects if an object ID doesn't actually exist
  if (is.null(data$features) || length(data$features) == 0) {
    return(tibble())
  }

  # Convert the returned object to a flat data frame, preserving both attributes and geometry
  rows <- lapply(data$features, function(feature) {
    attrs <- normalizeAttributes(feature$attributes)

    if (is.null(attrs)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    # Save the full ArcGIS geometry object as JSON text
    attrs$geometry_json <- if (is.null(feature$geometry)) {
      NA_character_
    } else {
      as.character(toJSON(feature$geometry, auto_unbox = TRUE, null = "null"))
    }

    attrs
  })

  # Filter out rows that are empty
  rows <- Filter(Negate(is.null), rows)

  # If all the rows were empty return an empty tibble
  if (length(rows) == 0) {
    return(tibble())
  }

  # Combine all the rows into a data frame and return it
  bind_rows(rows)
}

# Save a data frame to memory to allow for continuous data collection
saveChunk <- function(df, chunk_id, save_directory) {
  # File path to save
  file_path <- file.path(save_directory, sprintf("chunk_%05d.rds", chunk_id))

  # Save the file as a .rds file
  saveRDS(df, file_path)

  # Return the file path of the saved file
  file_path
}

# Combine all saved chunks into one data frame
combineChunks <- function(save_directory) {
  # Find all the files in the specified save directory
  files <- list.files(save_directory, pattern = "^chunk_[0-9]{5}\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)

  # If there are no files return an empty tibble
  if (length(files) == 0) {
    return(tibble())
  }

  # Combine the files into 1 data frame
  bind_rows(lapply(files, readRDS))
}

fetchParcels <- function(key, url, batch_size = 1000, out_fields = "*", save_directory, layerJson) {
  # Create a directory, showWarnings = FALSE makes it not show an error if the directory already exists and simply move on
  dir.create(save_directory, showWarnings = FALSE)

  ids <- getObjectIDs(url, layerJson)
  total_ids <- length(ids)
  
  # Split the object IDs into chunks. Arcgis allows for processing of 1000 object IDs in parallel
  chunks <- split(ids, ceiling(seq_along(ids) / batch_size)) 
  total_chunks <- length(chunks)

  # Print some information about the data set size
  message("County: ", key)
  message("Total parcel IDs: ", total_ids)
  message("Batch size: ", batch_size)
  message("Total chunks: ", total_chunks)

  # Find the completed chunks so that data isn't collected twice
  completed_files <- list.files(save_directory, pattern = "^chunk_[0-9]{5}\\.rds$")
  completed_ids <- as.integer(gsub("^chunk_([0-9]{5})\\.rds$", "\\1", completed_files))
  completed_ids <- completed_ids[!is.na(completed_ids)]

  # Find the completed IDs to add to progress bar
  already_done_ids <- sum(vapply(
    seq_along(chunks),
    function(i) if (i %in% completed_ids) length(chunks[[i]]) else 0L,
    integer(1)
  ))

# Create a progress bar to show how much of the data has been collected (mainly to make sure it is actually working as data collection takes a long time and I want to see if something is happening and it isn't stuck with some error)
  progress_bar <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = total_ids, style = 3)
  setTxtProgressBar(progress_bar, already_done_ids)

  # Loop through all of the chunks in the chunks object
  for (i in seq_along(chunks)) {
    # Create the file if it doesn't exist
    chunk_file <- file.path(save_directory, sprintf("chunk_%05d.rds", i))

    # If the file does exist move along so not overwriting data
    if (file.exists(chunk_file)) {
      next
    }

    # Part of the progress bar
    message("\nProcessing chunk ", i, " of ", total_chunks)

    # Fetch the chunk
    chunk_df <- fetchChunk(url, chunks[[i]], out_fields = out_fields, layerJson)

    # If the fetch was successful and returned data save it to file
    if (!is.null(chunk_df)) {
      saveChunk(chunk_df, i, save_directory)
    }

    # Part of the progress bar
    done_ids <- sum(vapply(
      seq_along(chunks),
      function(j) {
        f <- file.path(save_directory, sprintf("chunk_%05d.rds", j))
        if (file.exists(f)) length(chunks[[j]]) else 0L
      },
      integer(1)
    ))
    
    # Part of the progress bar
    setTxtProgressBar(progress_bar, done_ids)
  }
  
  # End the progress bar
  close(progress_bar)

}
```

Main Functions
```{r}
# Main function to download all of the parcel data and geometry
fetchParcels <- function(url, layer_id, batch_size = 1000, out_fields = "*", save_directory) {
  # Create a directory, showWarnings = FALSE makes it not show an error if the directory already exists and simply move on
  dir.create(save_directory, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  # Construct the layer JSON for dynamic queries
  layerJson <- makeLayerJson(layer_id)

  # Get the IDs from the requested county
  ids <- getObjectIDs(url, layerJson)
  total_ids <- length(ids)

  # Split the object IDs into chunks. Arcgis usually allows for processing of 1000-2000 object IDs in parallel
  chunks <- split(ids, ceiling(seq_along(ids) / batch_size))
  total_chunks <- length(chunks)

  # Print some information about the data set size
  message("Total parcel IDs: ", total_ids)
  message("Batch size: ", batch_size)
  message("Total chunks: ", total_chunks)

  # Find the completed chunks so that data isn't collected twice
  completed_files <- list.files(save_directory, pattern = "^chunk_[0-9]{5}\\.rds$")
  completed_ids <- as.integer(gsub("^chunk_([0-9]{5})\\.rds$", "\\1", completed_files))
  completed_ids <- completed_ids[!is.na(completed_ids)]

  # Find the completed IDs so that data isn't collected twice
  already_done_ids <- sum(vapply(
    seq_along(chunks),
    function(i) if (i %in% completed_ids) length(chunks[[i]]) else 0L,
    integer(1)
  ))

  # Create a progress bar to show how much of the data has been collected
  progress_bar <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = total_ids, style = 3)
  setTxtProgressBar(progress_bar, already_done_ids)

  # Loop through all of the chunks in the chunks object
  for (i in seq_along(chunks)) {
    # Create the file if it doesn't exist
    chunk_file <- file.path(save_directory, sprintf("chunk_%05d.rds", i))

    # If the file does exist move along so not overwriting data
    if (file.exists(chunk_file)) {
      next
    }

    # Part of the progress bar
    message("\nProcessing chunk ", i, " of ", total_chunks)

    # Fetch the chunk
    chunk_df <- tryCatch(
      fetchChunk(url, chunks[[i]], out_fields = out_fields, layerJson = layerJson),
      error = function(e) {
        message("Chunk ", i, " failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
        return(NULL)
      }
    )

    # If the fetch was successful and returned data save it to file
    if (!is.null(chunk_df)) {
      saveChunk(chunk_df, i, save_directory)
    }

    # Part of the progress bar
    done_ids <- sum(vapply(
      seq_along(chunks),
      function(j) {
        f <- file.path(save_directory, sprintf("chunk_%05d.rds", j))
        if (file.exists(f)) length(chunks[[j]]) else 0L
      },
      integer(1)
    ))

    # Part of the progress bar
    setTxtProgressBar(progress_bar, done_ids)
  }

  # End the progress bar
  close(progress_bar)

  # Return the combined county data
  combineChunks(save_directory)
}


# Get the first 5 entries for one county as sf data
fetchFirstFiveSF <- function(url, layer_id, out_fields = "*") {
  # Construct the layer JSON for dynamic queries
  layerJson <- makeLayerJson(layer_id)

  # Get the IDs from the requested county
  ids <- getObjectIDs(url, layerJson)

  # Keep only the first 5 IDs
  sample_ids <- ids

  # Fetch the first 5 entries as sf data
  fetchChunk(url, sample_ids, out_fields = out_fields, layerJson = layerJson)
}
```

```{r}
makeSampleChoropleth <- function(sf_object, county_name, output_file) {
  # Return NULL if there is nothing to map
  if (is.null(sf_object) || nrow(sf_object) == 0) {
    message("No sf data found for ", county_name)
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Transform the geometry to WGS84 for leaflet
  sf_object <- sf::st_transform(sf_object, 4326)

  # Pick a field for the choropleth
  fill_col <- pickChoroplethColumn(sf_object)

  # If no numeric field exists, make a fake index so the parcels still display
  if (is.null(fill_col)) {
    sf_object$map_value <- seq_len(nrow(sf_object))
    fill_col <- "map_value"
  }

  # Convert the map field to numeric for coloring
  sf_object[[fill_col]] <- as.numeric(sf_object[[fill_col]])

  # Create a color palette for the selected field
  pal <- colorNumeric(
    palette = "viridis",
    domain = sf_object[[fill_col]],
    na.color = "transparent"
  )

  # Create labels for the map
  labels <- paste0(
    county_name,
    "<br>",
    fill_col,
    ": ",
    sf_object[[fill_col]]
  )

  # Make the choropleth map
  map <- leaflet(sf_object) |>
    addTiles() |>
    addPolygons(
      fillColor = ~pal(.data[[fill_col]]),
      color = "black",
      weight = 1,
      opacity = 1,
      fillOpacity = 0.65,
      label = lapply(labels, htmltools::HTML)
    ) |>
    addLegend(
      pal = pal,
      values = sf_object[[fill_col]],
      title = fill_col
    )

  # Save the map to an html file
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(map, output_file, selfcontained = TRUE)

  # Return the map object
  map
}

# Pick a numeric column for the choropleth map
pickChoroplethColumn <- function(sf_object) {
  # Drop the geometry to inspect only attribute data
  attrs <- sf::st_drop_geometry(sf_object)

  # Find columns that are already numeric
  numeric_cols <- names(attrs)[vapply(attrs, is.numeric, logical(1))]

  # If there are numeric columns, use the first one
  if (length(numeric_cols) > 0) {
    return(numeric_cols[1])
  }

  # Find character columns that look numeric
  possible_numeric_cols <- names(attrs)[vapply(attrs, function(x) {
    non_na <- x[!is.na(x)]
    length(non_na) > 0 && all(str_detect(as.character(non_na), "^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$"))
  }, logical(1))]

  # If there are numeric-looking columns, convert and use the first one
  if (length(possible_numeric_cols) > 0) {
    return(possible_numeric_cols[1])
  }

  # If no usable column exists, return NULL
  NULL
}
```

```{r}
arcgisPolygonToSF <- function(geometry_json) {
  geom <- fromJSON(geometry_json, simplifyVector = FALSE)

  if (is.null(geom$rings)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  rings <- lapply(geom$rings, function(ring) {
    coords <- do.call(rbind, ring)
    coords <- matrix(as.numeric(coords), ncol = 2, byrow = FALSE)

    # Close ring if needed
    if (!all(coords[1, ] == coords[nrow(coords), ])) {
      coords <- rbind(coords, coords[1, ])
    }

    coords
  })

  st_polygon(rings)
}

files <- list.files(
  path = "Data2/",
  pattern = "\\.rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

owner_fields <- c(
  "TAO_NAME",
  "OWNER",
  "CurOwnerName",
  "OWNER_NAME",
  "OWNERNAME",
  "PROP_OWNER",
  "OWNERNAME1",
  "TAXPAYER_NAME1",
  "TAXPAYER_NAME",
  "OWNAME",
  "TAX_NAME",
  "Ownname",
  "dbo.tblManatronParcelInfo.TaxName",
  "OWNNAME",
  "OWNER_NM",
  "PINAME1",
  "OWNERNME1",
  "Full_Name",
  "OwnerName1",
  "OwnerName"
)

for (file in files) {

  dat <- readRDS(file)
  
  # Find matching owner column
  owner_col <- intersect(owner_fields, names(dat))

  # Standardize to OWNER_NAME
  if (length(owner_col) > 0) {
    dat <- dat |>
      rename(OWNER_NAME = all_of(owner_col[1]))
  } else {
    dat$OWNER_NAME <- NA_character_
  }

  geoms <- lapply(dat$geometry_json, arcgisPolygonToSF)

  valid <- !sapply(geoms, is.null)

  parcels_sf <- st_sf(
    dat[valid, ],
    geometry = st_sfc(geoms[valid], crs = 4326)
  )

  # County Name
  file_prefix <- sub("_.*$", "", basename(file))
  
  # Save individually
  saveRDS(
    parcels_sf,
    file = file.path("Data2/", paste0(file_prefix, "_parcels_sf.rds"))
  )
}
```

```{r}
`%||%` <- function(x, y) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) y else x
}

# Remove /query from the URL so metadata can be requested
getMetadataURL <- function(query_url) {
  str_replace(query_url, "/query$", "")
}

# Check whether a county supports historical ownership or geometry
checkHistoricalSupport <- function(county_name, url) {
  metadata_url <- getMetadataURL(url)

  response <- GET(
    metadata_url,
    query = list(f = "json"),
    timeout(120),
    user_agent("Mozilla/5.0")
  )

  stop_for_status(response)

  metadata <- fromJSON(
    content(response, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"),
    simplifyVector = FALSE
  )

  # Field metadata
  fields <- metadata$fields

  field_names <- vapply(
    fields,
    function(x) x$name %||% NA_character_,
    character(1)
  )

  field_types <- vapply(
    fields,
    function(x) x$type %||% NA_character_,
    character(1)
  )

  # Date fields
  date_fields <- field_names[field_types == "esriFieldTypeDate"]

  # Fields that imply ownership history
  history_fields <- grep(
    "SALE|DEED|OWNER|OWN|TRANSFER|DATE|YEAR|YR|EDIT|CREATE|UPDATE|HIST",
    field_names,
    ignore.case = TRUE,
    value = TRUE
  )

  # ArcGIS historical support
  has_time_info <- !is.null(metadata$timeInfo)

  supports_historic_moment <-
    metadata$advancedQueryCapabilities$supportsQueryWithHistoricMoment %||% FALSE

  supports_statistics <-
    metadata$advancedQueryCapabilities$supportsStatistics %||% FALSE

  tibble(
    county = county_name,
    layer_name = metadata$name %||% NA_character_,
    geometry_type = metadata$geometryType %||% NA_character_,
    has_timeInfo = has_time_info,
    supports_historic_moment = supports_historic_moment,
    has_date_fields = length(date_fields) > 0,
    date_fields = paste(date_fields, collapse = ", "),
    possible_history_fields = paste(history_fields, collapse = ", "),
    max_record_count = metadata$maxRecordCount %||% NA_integer_
  )
}
```

```{r}
history_support <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(urls), function(key) {
    tryCatch(
      checkHistoricalSupport(
        county_name = key,
        url = urls[[key]]$url
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        tibble(
          county = key,
          layer_name = NA_character_,
          geometry_type = NA_character_,
          has_timeInfo = NA,
          supports_historic_moment = NA,
          has_date_fields = NA,
          date_fields = NA_character_,
          possible_history_fields = paste(
            "FAILED:",
            conditionMessage(e)
          ),
          max_record_count = NA_integer_
        )
      }
    )
  })
)
```
